testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A CMV driver with a detectable amount of alcohol in their system (but below the legal limit) will receive:
questions.explanation: If you have any detectable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a CMV, even if your blood alcohol level is below 0.04 percent, you will be put out of service for 24 hours. Driving a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its cargo while keeping the axles in place. Broken parts in this system are extremely dangerous.

questions.question: On a long downhill slope, you should brake by:

options.text: Using the brakes mostly and downshifting occasionally.
Downshifting first, then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: On a long downgrade, shift into a lower gear first, then use proper braking. Using only the brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. A lower gear increases the engine's braking power, which is the main way to control your speed going downhill.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer:

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Place a heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Never open trailer doors during a cargo fire, especially if the cargo contains hazardous materials. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes it grow larger.

questions.question: For the on-road driving skills test:

options.text: You do not need to use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
The type of vehicle you use does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
questions.explanation: You must take the on-road skills test in the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.

questions.question: If a train is approaching a railroad crossing you are near, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. If you see a train approaching a crossing, stop and wait for it to pass before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: Cargo should be covered to:
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people from spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always make a complete stop.
May need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest choice.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Plan how to handle dangerous situations.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: While driving, constantly look for hazards. Plan what you will do if a hazard turns into an emergency.

questions.question: Wheel bearing/seals should be:
questions.explanation: During an inspection, make sure wheel bearing/seals are not leaking.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, you should keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle length.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, keep at least one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same rule and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: A five-foot-long item on a flatbed trailer must be secured with at least:
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. However, always use at least two tie-downs, no matter how small the cargo is.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you should check for all of the following, except:

options.text: Too much air pressure in your tires.
Too little air pressure in your tires.
The same tire brand on all tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same tire brand on all tires.
questions.explanation: Check that your tire air pressure is not too low or too high. The tire brand does not matter.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, first look for an escape ramp. If there is no ramp, find another safe place to stop, such as an open field or a road that goes uphill or becomes flat.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who does not know traffic rules.

questions.explanation: Watch for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick are dangerous. Stopping at a green light is one sign of impaired driving.

questions.question: You should check your cargo:

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every 3 hours or 150 miles. Check it every time you take a break. You are responsible for keeping cargo safe during the trip.

questions.question: Poor weight balance in a trailer:
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle unsafe to handle. Too much or too little weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Spread weight evenly from front to back and side to side, and place it as low as possible.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to help fuel reach the engine.
Let the air compressor build 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Begin driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while changing gears:

options.text: You may have trouble engaging the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble engaging the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long can make it hard to shift into the next gear. Do not force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match road speed, and try again.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Trust warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
Watch what other drivers do to see if a train is coming.
Do not depend only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not depend only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Do not rely only on warning signals, gates, or flaggers to warn you about trains. Watch especially carefully at crossings without gates or signals. At any railroad crossing, always assume a train is coming.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: The speed of the cars around you.
Much slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the cars around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. Cars moving at the same speed in the same direction are less likely to crash. However, never drive faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You are driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph. What is your minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same rule and add one more second.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating your large vehicle. What should you NOT do?

options.text: Increase the space between you and the car ahead.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your following distance and avoid sudden moves. Speeding up will not help—the other driver may just tailgate you at a higher speed. Do not flash your brake lights or turn on your taillights to signal the other driver.

questions.question: What happens when cargo is loaded with a high center of gravity?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
Items are more likely to fall down.
The cargo is harder to unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will roll over. Always load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones. Drive carefully and slowly near workers.

questions.question: Near a railroad crossing, what should you know about hearing trains?

options.text: You will hear every train that is coming.
You might not hear a train, even if one is coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You might not hear a train, even if one is coming.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear a train coming. The train operator may not sound the horn, or horns may not be allowed in some areas. Even if the horn sounds, noise inside your car may prevent you from hearing it until the train is very close.

questions.question: What can water on a roadway cause?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on a road surface.

questions.question: What happens after two violations for using a hand-held mobile phone while driving?

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
Your CDL will be taken away.
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your CDL will be taken away.
questions.explanation: Two convictions for using a hand-held mobile phone while driving will result in losing your CDL. Penalties become stricter with more violations.

questions.question: What is black ice?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like a wet road. Be alert for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: A 10-foot load must be secured with a minimum of:
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: Perform pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time because:

options.text: You will be less likely to forget something.
You will have more time to complete the inspection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order helps you learn the correct steps. You are less likely to skip a step when you follow a set order.

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: Do not decide when to shift gears based on:

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Do not base gear shifts on other vehicles' actions.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: Pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Tell other drivers you are angry.
Warn other drivers that you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are near.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others of your presence. Use it only when necessary, as it can startle other drivers.

questions.question: You are most likely to encounter strong winds when:
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially a problem when exiting a tunnel.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe to use on rear tires.
Are safe to use when carrying light loads.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: Which gas is dangerous if your exhaust system leaks?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system lets carbon monoxide, a poison, enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: A distracted driver:
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see road hazards more slowly than focused drivers, or may not see them at all.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. This applies no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations are not included.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, what happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly?

options.text: An extra point against your final score.
Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: You must always face the vehicle and keep three points of contact when exiting. If driving a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly results in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: In newer vehicles, how do you apply the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: Newer vehicles with air brakes use a yellow, diamond-shaped knob to control the parking brake. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: Where should the center of gravity be in a trailer?

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight as low as possible. A high center of gravity increases the risk of rollover.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do shortly after?

options.text: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After a short period of driving, stop and recheck that all lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended, can you get a hardship license to drive a CMV?

options.text: Yes, you can get a hardship license to operate a CMV.
No, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a CMV.
Your CDL will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a CMV.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a CMV.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It takes your attention and hands off the road.
A message may upset the driver.
People may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your attention and hands off the road.
questions.explanation: Texting is dangerous because it is both a mental and physical distraction. It diverts your mind from the road and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. If one system has a leak, it may not affect the other system.

questions.question: What is the only way to become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers and coffee do not speed this up. Only time will allow your body to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: You are driving slowly through a construction zone and see a construction worker near the road. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Always slow down in construction zones. Reduce your speed even further if workers are on or near the road.
